title: Human report semantic quality
outOfScope: Changing provider configuration or treating local/repository claims as provider evidence.
Changing Task Outcome fact collection outside report projection needs.

sources.reason: WI-09 required report structure, prohibited claims, and ordinary-user acceptance questions.
Current Human Benefit Report projection and validation boundary.
Existing focused report behavior and regression coverage.

riskAssessment.reason: A report is the human decision surface; ambiguous completion and missing limitations can cause unsafe reliance.

reasons: Human-facing evidence interpretation and forced-stop semantics are high-impact governance boundaries.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized the governed lifecycle; implementation is limited to truthful report projection and tests.

preReviewWarnings: Review that each fixed human question has a direct, evidence-derived answer and no prohibited claim can appear with missing evidence.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The Human Benefit Report renders the twelve required sections: conclusion, completed work, findings, interventions, forced stops, resolved risks, avoided impact, unresolved risks, not-run verification, prohibited claims, human decisions, and next step.
The report cannot say all complete, safe, enterprise-grade, tested, user-approved, or avoided major risk unless source-bound evidence supports the exact claim.
Focused tests cover not_run, fixture-only, missing approval binding, unsupported safety and enterprise claims, and ordinary-user questions without JSON inspection.
Documentation explains report semantics and the limits of the rendered decision surface.
guidelines: Every report statement must be derived from validated Task Outcome facts or explicitly marked unavailable.
Do not convert warning, local, fixture, repository-recorded, or missing evidence into a stronger claim.
Keep the report concise enough for an ordinary user while retaining actionable stop and recovery facts.
Document all public report semantics and prohibited claims.

intent.problem: Existing reports expose internal fields but do not reliably tell a person what was completed, what was blocked, what may not be claimed, or who must decide next.
constraints: Preserve Task Outcome as the evidence authority.
Never infer external provider, enterprise, approval, safety, or causal-risk evidence.
Make unavailable and forced-stop facts visible without requiring JSON inspection.
Keep focused tests deterministic and report generation local.
intent.rationale: A stable evidence-derived report lets people make calibrated continuation decisions without mistaking formatted output for proof.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: ordinary user answers the required questions without JSON
scenarioCoverage.expected: Rendered report states completed work, omissions, blocks, rationale, continuation state, and decision owner.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused rendering tests with complete and constrained Task Outcomes.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: not_run or missing evidence blocks completion and safety overclaims
scenarioCoverage.expected: Report names unavailable verification and prohibited claims instead of saying all complete or safe.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: fixture and repository assertions cannot become provider or approval evidence
scenarioCoverage.expected: Report preserves fixture/local/repository evidence limits and shows approval as unavailable without a binding.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused evidence-level and approval-binding tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: forced stops, residual risk, human decision, and next step remain actionable
scenarioCoverage.expected: Each constrained outcome renders intervention, responsible decision owner, and safe continuation direction.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run report rendering regressions for blocked and warning states.
